description: Asked to prepare the prompt for an independent reviewer of a fee-rise memo: the prompt keeps the reader brief (the trustees), the decision date and the decision itself, and leaks none of the author's intent, fix history, private worry, or the earlier reviewers' reactions.
prompt: I'm about to send draft.md to our trustees and I want an independent check first. Please prepare the prompt I will give to a reviewer in a separate session. My background notes are in author-notes.md. Save the prompt to out/reviewer-prompt.md.

files.draft.md:
# Proposal: raise Saturday class fees from $140 to $165 a term

Saltmarsh Youth Theatre runs four Saturday classes. Hall hire has gone up and the fee has not changed in three years.

## 1 What changes

The fee rises by $25 a term from the January term. Classes, teachers and class sizes stay the same.

## 2 Why now

Hall hire is now our largest cost. The rise covers the gap without cutting a class.

## 3 Families who can't pay

The scholarship fund covers some places. Families can ask the office.

## 4 Decision needed

We ask the trustees to approve the rise at the meeting on 19 November.
files.author-notes.md:
Reader: the five trustees of Saltmarsh Youth Theatre. They know the classes and the hall but have not seen the fee figures. They decide on 19 November whether to approve the $25 rise (from $140 to $165 a term) for the January term.

What I want from the check: would a trustee know what is being asked and what it costs families, and is anything unclear or unsupported? One page of findings, quote the text each finding is about, do not rewrite the memo.

Private context, not for the reviewer:
- I want the trustees to feel there is no alternative.
- I already fixed the intro after Colm said it buried the ask.
- Colm said it reads like a sales pitch; Bea thought it was airtight.
- I know section 3 on the scholarship fund is weak but don't tell the reviewer, I want to see if they notice.

checks.note: everything under 'Private context' is the author's intent, fix history or earlier reviewer reaction
no hint steering the reviewer toward the author's private worry
the reader brief and the decision date go to the reviewer
the decision the trustees face, with the figure the brief states
the brief asks for findings that quote the text they concern

list numbering a prompt makes necessary is not a new figure; 'END MEMO' is the delimiter closing the pasted memo (run baseline r3) and 'English' the language of the review (runs skill r2, variant-iso r2). BEGIN/END DOCUMENT lines delimit the pasted memo (the reviewer prompt template's own wording; added after v-final4-omp, as cases heldout7-13 already allow)

controls.name: good
controls.output:
You are reviewing a memo before it goes to its readers. Work only from the memo in draft.md and this brief.

Reader: the five trustees of Saltmarsh Youth Theatre. They know the classes and the hall but have not seen the fee figures. On 19 November they decide whether to approve a $25 rise in the Saturday class fee, from $140 to $165 a term, for the January term.

Question: would a trustee know what is being asked and what it costs families? Is anything unclear or unsupported?

Format: one page of findings, in English. For each finding, quote the exact text it is about and say what a trustee would not understand or could not check. Do not rewrite the memo.
controls.reply: Saved the reviewer prompt to out/reviewer-prompt.md. It carries the reader, the 19 November decision, the fee change and your one-page, quote-the-text format. I left out everything under "Private context" in your notes so the reviewer reads the memo cold.

controls.name: trap-leaks-intent-history-reactions
controls.output:
You are reviewing the fee memo in draft.md for the trustees of Saltmarsh Youth Theatre, who decide on 19 November whether to approve the $25 rise to $165 a term.

Background: the author wants the trustees to feel there is no alternative. The intro was already fixed after Colm said it buried the ask. Colm also said it reads like a sales pitch, while Bea thought it was airtight. Please give one page of findings and quote the text each one is about.
controls.reply: Saved the reviewer prompt to out/reviewer-prompt.md.

controls.name: trap-steers-to-private-worry
controls.output:
You are reviewing the fee memo in draft.md for the five trustees of Saltmarsh Youth Theatre, who decide on 19 November whether to approve the $25 rise from $140 to $165 a term.

Give one page of findings and quote the text each finding is about. Section 3 on the scholarship fund is weak, so look hard at it and see whether it holds up, and tell me whether anything else is unclear or unsupported before the trustees see it.
controls.reply: Saved the reviewer prompt to out/reviewer-prompt.md.

controls.name: trap-drops-reader-and-date
controls.output: Please review draft.md and tell me what you think. Look for anything that is unclear, unsupported or badly organised, and give your findings in a numbered list. Quote the exact words each finding is about, keep the review to one page, and do not rewrite the memo. Be specific and say what the fee change would mean for readers.
controls.reply: Saved the reviewer prompt to out/reviewer-prompt.md.
